H96: 1996 table, category (c), Micturin row and footnote. Year of market removal, not precise legal effective date.
Hletter: Retrospective CSM communications list: 25 July 1991 terodiline and adverse cardiac reactions. Not a substitute for the unseen original letter.
Connolly: Author metadata and primary abstract. Five patients, four women; mean 74 years, range 55–87. TdP and QT prolongation; baseline QT normal in three, normalized off drug in four; bradycardia or AV conduction disturbance in all.
McLeod: June 1991 BMJ report, title/author/DOI metadata: TdP complicating treatment with terodiline.
Stewart: 1992 abstract: four cases, two hypokalaemic on diuretics; separate eight elderly inpatients, 12.5 mg BID seven days, mean QT +29 ms, QTc +15 ms, resting HR −6.7/min.
Thomas: 1995 original abstract, subjects/methods/results: stable-dose asymptomatic patients; increased QTc and dispersion correlated with total and both enantiomer concentrations. Not a TdP incidence study.
IKr: 1998 original abstract: guinea-pig ventricular myocytes, E4031-sensitive native IKr IC50 0.7 µM. Higher concentrations also affect IKs.
IK1: 1999 original abstract: separate native outward IK1 IC50 7 µM; not IKr.
Dog: 2001 abstract, dog action-potential duration versus concentrations: not a selective direct-current measurement.
Racemate: 1996 randomized single-dose volunteer study of racemate and enantiomers, not metabolites; QTc increase with racemate and R(+).
Genotype: 2000 primary study of genotypes in eight survivors identified via a UK reporting system, not a population absolute-risk estimate.
HEK: 2006 primary comparison, hERG in HEK at 37 C: terodiline IC50 375 nM; distinction from native IKr 0.7 µM and different Purkinje outcomes.

PMID:12709719.finding: In a randomized, four-period crossover study in healthy adults, single doses of moxifloxacin 800 mg, levofloxacin 1,000 mg and ciprofloxacin 1,500 mg were compared with placebo. The reported mean 24-hour QTc changes using Bazett correction were 16.34–17.83 ms, 3.53–4.88 ms and 2.27–4.93 ms, respectively. These ranges reflect different baseline methods; they are not confidence intervals.
PMID:12709719.limitations: The study used high single exposures. Baseline method and daily variation affected the estimates. Clinical-event relevance was not established. The complete original abstract was inspected; the full methods and tables were not independently inspected.
PMID:12709719.source_with_locator: [PMID:12709719](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12709719/). Locator: Abstract > METHODS; RESULTS; CONCLUSIONS. Access depth: complete original abstract inspected.

PMID:16472283.finding: Thirteen healthy participants received ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily, levofloxacin 500 mg daily and moxifloxacin 400 mg daily in an open-label crossover study with randomized treatment order. Each course lasted seven days, with a one-week washout. Lead II QTc was assessed before treatment, two hours after the first dose and after the course. Moxifloxacin increased QTc by 6 ms from baseline; no QTc effect was detected for ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin, and no QT-dispersion change was detected.
PMID:16472283.limitations: This small surrogate-endpoint study does not establish absence of torsades de pointes or safety with other QT-active medicines. The exact correction formula and numerical full-text tables are excluded from mandatory gold because their original passages were not inspected.
PMID:16472283.source_with_locator: [PMID:16472283](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16472283/). Locator: Abstract > Methods; Results and Conclusions. Access depth: complete original abstract inspected.

PMID:16304291.finding: This US multicentre, randomized, double-blind trial enrolled 394 patients aged at least 65 years with community-acquired pneumonia. Treatment was moxifloxacin 400 mg or levofloxacin 500 mg daily, intravenously or orally, for 7–14 days. The Holter composite occurred in 16/192 versus 10/195 patients (P=.29), mainly as nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. One torsades event occurred in the levofloxacin arm. Day-three QTcF changes were +6.4±23.2 versus −2.5±22.9 ms.
PMID:16304291.limitations: There was no ciprofloxacin arm. A nonsignificant difference is not proof of equivalence, and this result does not establish safety for every concomitant-medication combination.

PMID:30269062.finding: A Korean claims cohort from 2015 compared oral fluoroquinolones with cefixime. During days 1–7, the moxifloxacin odds ratio for serious ventricular arrhythmia was 1.87 (95% CI 1.15–3.11), based on seven events. No increased association was detected for ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin. The study excluded exposure to QT- or torsades-associated drugs during the 30 days before through the 30 days after the index date.
PMID:30269062.limitations: Residual confounding, claims-based endpoints, absence of ECG and laboratory measurements, and the small moxifloxacin event count limit inference. The exclusion criterion prevents direct extrapolation to patients already using QT-active medicines.
PMID:30269062.source_with_locator: [PMID:30269062](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6169761/). Locator: Full text: Methods, Inclusion criteria/exposures (s2c), Exclusion criteria (s2d), Outcome (s2e); Results (s3b), Table 2; Limitations (s4d).. Access depth: primary full text inspected.

PMID:26920666.finding: This Danish and Swedish propensity-matched cohort compared oral fluoroquinolones with penicillin V. Most fluoroquinolone exposure was ciprofloxacin. The rate ratio for serious arrhythmia during current use was 0.85 (95% CI 0.61–1.18).
PMID:26920666.limitations: The drug mix was dominated by ciprofloxacin. This null estimate does not prove equivalence or establish the risk of every individual fluoroquinolone or high-risk drug combination.

PMID:23229485.finding: This retrospective study included 94 haematology inpatients receiving a fluoroquinolone with an azole: 88 received levofloxacin, 53 voriconazole and 40 fluconazole. Mean QTc change was 6.1 ms (95% CI 0.2–11.9). Twenty-one patients (22.3%) met the study criteria for a clinically significant QTc change. Hypokalaemia and left ventricular ejection fraction below 55% were associated with these changes.
PMID:23229485.limitations: The 22.3% result concerns QTc changes, not torsades incidence. The trend with multiple QT-active drugs was not statistically significant. The study does not establish a causal drug ranking or a drug-specific interaction risk ratio. Exact full-text threshold definitions are not mandatory gold in this abstract-bounded review.

PMID:22591294.finding: The Tennessee Medicaid cohort included patients aged 30–74 years and 347,795 azithromycin prescriptions. Over five days, cardiovascular-death hazard was higher than with amoxicillin: HR 2.49 (95% CI 1.38–4.50). The estimated excess was 47 cardiovascular deaths per million courses, rising to 245 per million in the highest decile of baseline cardiovascular risk.
PMID:22591294.limitations: This was an observational study in a selected population. Indication, comparator selection and residual health differences may confound the association. Prescription courses are not unique patients. The comparison with no antibiotic addresses a different contrast from the comparison with amoxicillin.

PMID:23635050.finding: This nationwide Danish historical cohort covered adults aged 18–64 years during 1997–2010. Over five days, the cardiovascular-death rate ratio for azithromycin was 2.85 (95% CI 1.13–7.24) versus no antibiotic, but 0.93 (0.56–1.55) versus penicillin V. The adjusted difference versus penicillin V was −1 cardiovascular death per million episodes (95% CI −9 to 11).
PMID:23635050.limitations: The population and active comparator differ from those in Ray et al. The null active-comparator estimate does not establish zero risk. The original abstract was inspected; detailed full-text covariates and tables are not mandatory gold.
PMID:23635050.source_with_locator: [PMID:23635050](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23635050/). Locator: Abstract > Methods; Results; Conclusions. Access depth: complete original abstract inspected.

PMID:24615307.finding: In this US veterans outpatient cohort, days 1–5 hazard ratios versus amoxicillin were 1.48 (95% CI 1.05–2.09) for death and 1.77 (1.20–2.62) for serious arrhythmia with azithromycin. The corresponding levofloxacin estimates were 2.49 (1.70–3.64) and 2.43 (1.56–3.79). During days 6–10, levofloxacin estimates remained elevated at 1.95 (1.32–2.88) for death and 1.75 (1.09–2.82) for arrhythmia; azithromycin estimates were not statistically significant.
PMID:24615307.limitations: The measured death endpoint must not be relabelled as specifically cardiovascular death. Different indications and treatment durations, and residual confounding, prevent a causal head-to-head ranking from the two common-comparator estimates. Uninspected absolute-event tables are excluded from mandatory gold.

PMID:23360890.finding: The electronic-health-record study included 38,397 adults with an ECG 14–90 days after a prescription. Adjusted dose–QTc associations were detected for citalopram, escitalopram and amitriptyline. Within-person citalopram changes were +7.8 ms (SE 3.6) for 10 to 20 mg, and +10.3 ms (SE 4.0) for 20 to 40 mg.
PMID:23360890.limitations: Treatment, dose and ECG ascertainment were not randomized. The ECG sample was older and less healthy than patients without ECG data. Cross-sectional and within-person estimates must remain distinct. Null findings for other drugs do not prove absence of risk, and these QTc results do not estimate an individual torsades probability.

PMID:7526675.finding: The available abstract reports before-and-after comparisons in three groups of 26 patients with cardiac disease or arrhythmias receiving amiodarone, sematilide or sotalol. PMID:7526675.limitations: The indexed original abstract is explicitly truncated. The full paper’s doses, timing, randomization details and complete outcome collection were not independently verified. Dispersion findings do not establish comparative clinical torsades incidence. Numerical QTc-dispersion units are not required gold, and the review must not claim that the full study measured no clinical events.

PMID:7526675.finding: The available abstract reports before-and-after comparisons in three groups of 26 patients with cardiac disease or arrhythmias receiving amiodarone, sematilide or sotalol. All three prolonged QT and QTc. Only amiodarone reduced QT and QTc dispersion, including in the myocardial-infarction subgroup.
PMID:7526675.limitations: The indexed original abstract is explicitly truncated. The full paper’s doses, timing, randomization details and complete outcome collection were not independently verified. Dispersion findings do not establish comparative clinical torsades incidence. Numerical QTc-dispersion units are not required gold, and the review must not claim that the full study measured no clinical events.

SPL:56879738-8662-4f5c-8386-761ab2b5e46f.finding: The selected oral sotalol label identifies reduced creatinine clearance, female sex, higher dose, bradycardia, ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation, and heart failure as torsades risk factors. It specifies electrolyte correction, renal-function-based dosing and ECG precautions. It recommends avoiding other QT-prolonging medicines, a washout of at least three half-lives for class I or III antiarrhythmics, and no concomitant class IA or III treatment.

SPL:57f7f2ea-4ca9-4ada-e063-6294a90a492b.finding: The selected oral amiodarone label recommends avoiding QT-prolonging medicines. Negative chronotropes can worsen bradycardia, and interactions may persist for weeks to months after discontinuation. The label calls for correction of potassium, magnesium and calcium abnormalities and describes metabolic interactions. The 2–5% worsened-arrhythmia figure is not a torsades-specific incidence. Sotalol’s renal-clearance dosing rule must not be transferred to amiodarone.
